plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 10: Fixed-Axis Rotation
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional diagram of the torque produced by a force acting at a point away from the origin. Thin black axes labeled x toward the lower left, y to the right, and z upward meet at a point marked O. A heavy blue arrow labeled r, with an overhead vector arrow, runs from O down and to the right to a black dot labeled P. At P a red arrow labeled F points to the right and slightly upward, and a dashed line extends the line of r past P; the angle between that dashed extension and F is marked theta, with the same angle theta repeated on the far side of F where the dashed line of action continues to the lower right. A thin segment from near the origin meets that dashed line at a small right-angle square and is labeled r_perp. An orange arrow labeled tau rises straight up from P, standing perpendicular to the plane that holds r and F. Below and to the left, a drawn open right hand repeats the same blue r and red F arrows with curved black arrows wrapping around them to indicate the sense in which the fingers curl. Showing the geometric construction and the hand together supplies both the magnitude of the cross product, fixed by r, F, and theta, and its direction, which here lies along the positive z-axis.

elements: thin black x-axis pointing toward lower-left (out of screen toward viewer), labeled 'x' with arrowhead
thin black y-axis pointing right (horizontal), labeled 'y' with arrowhead
thin black z-axis pointing straight up, labeled 'z' with arrowhead
origin point labeled 'O' where the three axes meet (upper-left of frame)
heavy dark-blue arrow r from O running down-and-right to point P, labeled with vector symbol r
black dot at P with italic label 'P' just below it
red arrow F starting at P, pointing right and slightly upward, labeled with vector symbol F
black dashed line through P along the line of action of F, extending on both sides of P (to lower-right beyond F's tail region and back toward the left past P)
black dashed extension of r beyond/behind P toward the left (the dashed segment on which the near-side theta arc is drawn)
angle arc theta between the dashed extension of r and the red F arrow, on the left side of P
second angle arc theta on the right side of F, between F and the dashed line-of-action continuing to lower right
thin black line segment r_perp from near the origin to the line of action of F, meeting it at a right angle
small right-angle square marker where r_perp meets the line of action
italic label 'r⊥' beside the perpendicular segment
orange arrow tau rising vertically from P parallel to +z, labeled with vector symbol tau
right-hand-rule overlay: drawn open right hand at lower left with thumb along r
duplicate dark-blue r arrow in the hand overlay running down-and-right
duplicate red F arrow in the hand overlay pointing right and slightly upward
two curved black arrows wrapping around the overlay vectors showing the finger-curl sense of rotation

interactions.teaches: torque magnitude follows |r||F|sin(theta): the moment arm r_perp and the orange tau arrow grow to a maximum at 90 degrees and collapse to zero when F is parallel or antiparallel to r
interactions.label: Angle θ between r and F

interactions.teaches: the cross product needs two separate facts: the geometric construction gives the magnitude via the moment arm, while the right-hand rule fixes the direction of tau along +z
interactions.label: Overlay

interactions.teaches: r and F lie in one plane while tau stands perpendicular to that plane — only rotating the scene makes the out-of-plane direction unambiguous

demo_steps.title: Torque at an oblique angle
demo_steps.narration: The force F acts at P, a distance r from the origin. The perpendicular distance r⊥ from O to the line of action sets the moment arm, and tau points straight up along +z.

demo_steps.title: Maximum torque at 90°
demo_steps.narration: Rotating F until it is perpendicular to r makes r⊥ equal to the full length of r; the orange tau arrow reaches its longest.

demo_steps.title: Zero torque when aligned
demo_steps.narration: With F along the line of r, the line of action passes through O, r⊥ shrinks to zero and the tau arrow vanishes.

demo_steps.title: Right-hand rule fixes the direction
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the hand overlay: fingers curl from r toward F and the thumb points along +z, matching the orange tau arrow.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units: axes drawn from O at origin — y-axis +6 to the right, z-axis +5 up, x-axis +5 toward the lower-left/viewer (screen-down-left diagonal). r and F both lie in the horizontal x–y plane so that tau = r × F points along +z. r = (1.4, 3.2, 0), magnitude ≈3.5, drawn as a thick dark-blue shaft (radius ~0.06) with a cone head; P sits at that endpoint, roughly mid-right of the frame and below the y-axis. F has magnitude 2.2 and lies in the x–y plane at angle θ measured from the forward extension of r, rotated in the sense that gives r × F = +z; at the default θ≈35° it renders pointing right and slightly up-screen. Dashed black line of action runs through P along ±F for ±3.5 units; dashed extension of r runs 1.5 units past and behind P. r⊥ is the perpendicular dropped from O onto the line of action: length |r| sin θ ≈ 2.0 at default, drawn as a thin black line with a 0.22-unit right-angle square at its foot. tau drawn from P straight up, length = |r||F| sin θ scaled by 0.45 (≈1.9 at default, max ≈3.5 at 90°), orange shaft with cone head. Angle arcs: radius 0.7 for the near-side θ (between dashed r-extension and F) and radius 0.9 for the far-side θ (between F and the dashed line of action continuing lower-right). Right-hand overlay sits at roughly (3.5, -1.2, -1.5) in world space, i.e. lower-left of P, with a duplicate blue r arrow along the same direction as the main r and a duplicate red F arrow, plus two curved black arrows (torus arcs, ~0.5 radius) wrapping the vectors clockwise-as-seen-from-+z-above. Colors: axes and labels black #000000; r dark navy blue #1F3A66; F red #C8342C; tau orange #F5A11E; dashed lines black at 60% opacity; hand skin tone #F2C9A0 with #D9A77C outline; background white.
interactionPlan.notes: Build with Three.js using ArrowHelper-style custom arrows (CylinderGeometry shaft + ConeGeometry head) so shaft thickness can differ per vector (r thickest, F medium, tau medium, r⊥ thinnest as a plain Line). Use LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances() for the line-of-action and r-extension. Axis and vector labels as CSS2DRenderer sprites with italic serif styling and overhead vector arrows rendered as HTML (r⃗). Angle arcs via THREE.EllipseCurve rebuilt each frame in the x–y plane, anchored at P. The right-angle square at the foot of r⊥ is a small two-segment polyline in the r/F plane. Recompute r⊥, both arcs, and tau length live from the θ slider in a single update() so nothing drifts out of sync. Hand overlay: a simple low-poly stylized hand (or a textured plane billboard of the source hand illustration) shown only in 'Right-hand rule' mode, cross-fading with the r⊥/arc group; when active, pulse-highlight the curl arrows and the tau arrow together with an emissive boost. Keep OrbitControls damped, target on the midpoint of r, and clamp polar angle to keep the z-axis upright.

authoredContext:
When a force F→ is applied to a point P whose position is r→ relative to O (the figure), the torque τ→ around O is

The cross product r→×F→ also tells us the sign of the torque. In the figure, the cross product r→×F→ is along the positive z-axis, which by convention is a positive torque. If r→×F→ is along the negative z-axis, this produces a negative torque.

Now let’s consider how to define torques in the general three-dimensional case.

The torque is perpendicular to the plane defined by r→andF→ and its direction is determined by the right-hand rule.

Figure shows an XYZ coordinate system. Force F is applied in the XY plane and is parallel to the X axis. Vector r lies in the XY plane. It starts at the origin of the origin of the coordinate system and ends at the beginning of vector F. Vector for torque starts at the intersection point of r and v vectors. It is perpendicular to the XY plane and is pointed into the Z direction.

discrepancies: Camera/projection differs noticeably: in the source the y-axis runs horizontally to the right and the r–F plane reads clearly, while the render tips both x and y steeply downward so the horizontal plane is heavily foreshortened and the navy r vector looks short and nearly vertical instead of a long arrow reaching out along +y.

The whole figure occupies a small fraction of the canvas (auto-fit appears to include the hidden hand overlay bounds), leaving the axes, vectors and annotations far smaller and less legible than in the source.
The τ label renders as 'τ□' — the combining vector-arrow glyph falls back to a tofu box; other vector labels (r, F) also lose their over-arrows compared to the bold arrowed symbols in the source.

The right-hand / hand overlay with its duplicate r and F arrows and the two curl arrows (a prominent lower half of the source figure) is not visible in the default state; it exists only behind the 'Right-hand rule' toggle, so the default view drops roughly half of the source composition.
The r⊥ moment-arm line, its right-angle square and the two θ arcs are drawn but are so small/faint at the default framing that they barely register, whereas they are clearly emphasized in the source.
evaluation.notes: Conceptually correct and richly interactive torque figure (θ slider, geometric/right-hand overlays, guided demo, hover explanations), but the framing is too small and the axis projection too steep, so it reads as a shrunken, foreshortened version of the source with tofu glyphs in the τ label and the hand panel hidden by default.
action_items: Reframe the camera closer to the source axonometric (y roughly horizontal to the right, x toward the lower-left, z vertical) and compute the auto-fit only over the visible geometry so the figure fills the canvas rather than sitting at ~30% of its width.

Fix the vector label glyphs: use a styled overline/SVG arrow instead of the U+20D7 combining arrow so τ, r and F all show proper vector notation, and increase label font sizes for the primary vector labels relative to the axis labels.
Increase visual weight of the geometric construction (r⊥ line, right-angle mark, θ arcs, dashed line of action) so they remain readable at default zoom, matching their prominence in the source.
Consider showing a small always-visible hand/curl cue, or default the demo to briefly reveal the right-hand overlay, so the lower half of the source figure is represented at first glance.

Right-hand overlay sits at roughly (3.5, -1.2, -1.5) in world space, i.e. lower-left of P, with a duplicate blue r arrow along the same direction as the main r and a duplicate red F arrow, plus two curved black arrows (torus arcs, ~0.5 radius) wrapping the vectors clockwise-as-seen-from-+z-above. Colors: axes and labels black #000000; r dark navy blue #1F3A66; F red #C8342C; tau orange #F5A11E; dashed lines black at 60% opacity; hand skin tone #F2C9A0 with #D9A77C outline; background white.
interactionPlan.notes: Build with Three.js using ArrowHelper-style custom arrows (CylinderGeometry shaft + ConeGeometry head) so shaft thickness can differ per vector (r thickest, F medium, tau medium, r⊥ thinnest as a plain Line). Use LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances() for the line-of-action and r-extension. Axis and vector labels as CSS2DRenderer sprites with italic serif styling and overhead vector arrows rendered as HTML (r⃗). Angle arcs via THREE.EllipseCurve rebuilt each frame in the x–y plane, anchored at P. The right-angle square at the foot of r⊥ is a small two-segment polyline in the r/F plane. Recompute r⊥, both arcs, and tau length live from the θ slider in a single update() so nothing drifts out of sync. Hand overlay: a simple low-poly stylized hand (or a textured plane billboard of the source hand illustration) shown only in 'Right-hand rule' mode, cross-fading with the r⊥/arc group; when active, pulse-highlight the curl arrows and the tau arrow together with an emissive boost. Keep OrbitControls damped, target on the midpoint of r, and clamp polar angle to keep the z-axis upright.
